_comment: Where each model's files come from, and -- the part that matters -- WHICH
OF THEM CAN ACTUALLY BE DOWNLOADED AS AN ONNX EXPORT.
READ models/DOWNLOADS.md for the generated document; this file is its only
source, so the document cannot drift from this. tools/gen_downloads_doc.py
reads this AND models/<name>/CHECKPOINT.json, and REFUSES to write the
document if the two disagree about a digest, a repo or a file list.
THE CENTRAL FACT, AND THE ONE NOBODY HAD WRITTEN DOWN. SEVENTEEN of these
eighteen models have a checkpoint on HuggingFace; yolov8n-pose does not.
EIGHT of them ALSO publish an ONNX export you can download directly. THE
OTHER TEN DO NOT -- there is no onnx/ directory in the repository at all, and
asking for one returns 404.
That is the real reason BUILD.md 2.2 says 'weights are not fetched, you
place them': for ten of the eighteen there is nothing to fetch, because the
graph has to be produced by exporting the checkpoint. MEASURED on
verified_on by listing each repository's files; the `verified` field below
records what was actually DOWNLOADED AND HASHED, which is a stronger check
than a listing, because a listing proves a name exists and not that the bytes
behind it are the bytes this tree was built against.
THE COUNTS ABOVE ARE NOT TRUSTED: gen_downloads_doc.py recomputes both from
the rows below and prints them, so if a row is added or removed the prose
digest_kind says which of two DIFFERENT conventions that model's
CHECKPOINT.json uses, because they are not interchangeable:
model_digest -- tools/lib/onnx_weights.py model_digest(): sha256 over
(basename, NUL, sha256-of-file, LF) for each ONNX source
file, combined in a fixed order. NOT the sha256 of any one
file. This is what the single-string `sha256` in every
transformer CHECKPOINT.json holds.
file_sha256  -- a LIST of plain per-file sha256s, one per entry in `file`.
Only the two MediaPipe models write this shape.
Reading one as the other is a silent verification bypass: `1fd2e85d...` (what
bge-small-en-v1.5 records) is NOT the sha256 of its model.onnx, whose actual
hash is `828e1496...` -- both were measured here.
`onnx` is null when no ONNX export exists upstream. `export_note` then says
what a reader has to do instead, and it is deliberately NOT a command this
tree can run: no exporter for these nine lives here, and writing one is a
separate piece of work from listing where the files are.

embeddinggemma-300m.license_source: the MIRROR's license: tag -- and it agrees with Google's, so the Gemma terms still apply to this mirror
embeddinggemma-300m.pin_note: This is a THIRD-PARTY export, not the model's own repository, and it is a DIFFERENT SERIALISATION of the same weights -- so the recorded model_digest in CHECKPOINT.json will NOT match what you download, even when the packed container comes out identical. Re-record the pin from the file you actually placed; do not "correct" the recorded one to fit. Measured on whisper-tiny: the mirror's onnx files hash differently (encoder 8dd994fe..., decoder 7e844cce... against the tree's 6642befb.../ab79e3f2...) while the container's whole weight region is byte-identical (sha256 9fd75f76...). This mirror's model.onnx is 480 KB and its weights live in model.onnx_data, so it is a TWO-file download and the packer needs the side file beside the graph under exactly that name.

repo_disagreement.what: THREE repositories are in play and they are not interchangeable. runtime/src/common/hub.cpp fetches google/embeddinggemma-300m. models/embeddinggemma-300m/CHECKPOINT.json records unsloth/embeddinggemma-300m. The onnx/ graph comes from a third, onnx-community/embeddinggemma-300m-ONNX.
repo_disagreement.why_it_matters: Google's repository is GATED -- it needs HF_TOKEN and a licence accepted -- and hub.cpp fails closed rather than falling back to a mirror. The unsloth copy is ungated and holds the same weights. The onnx-community repository carries no model weights at all, only the export, and it too is tagged gemma. So a reader who needs no token should take unsloth's safetensors plus onnx-community's graph; a reader who runs `serve` takes Google's and is stopped without a token.
repo_disagreement.which_is_cited_here: The licence is Google's because that is whose terms the weights are under. All three are named; none is presented as another.

whisper-tiny.license_source: the MIRROR carries NO license: tag; the original openai/whisper-* tag says apache-2.0
whisper-tiny.pin_note: This is a THIRD-PARTY export, not the model's own repository, and it is a DIFFERENT SERIALISATION of the same weights -- so the recorded model_digest in CHECKPOINT.json will NOT match what you download, even when the packed container comes out identical. Re-record the pin from the file you actually placed; do not "correct" the recorded one to fit. Measured on whisper-tiny: the mirror's onnx files hash differently (encoder 8dd994fe..., decoder 7e844cce... against the tree's 6642befb.../ab79e3f2...) while the container's whole weight region is byte-identical (sha256 9fd75f76...). Two files, and they are not interchangeable: the decoder without past-KV state is a different graph from decoder_model_merged.onnx, which the same repository also publishes. This tree reads onnx/decoder_model.onnx -- see runtime/include/common/onnx_read.hpp kWhisperDecoderOnnx -- so take that one.
whisper-tiny.verified: BOTH files downloaded and hashed, and the container PACKED: its entire weight region is byte-identical to the one this tree built (sha256 9fd75f76...), from input files that hash differently (encoder 8dd994fe..., decoder 7e844cce...). So the weights are the same and the serialisation is not -- see `pin_note`, because that is the fact that makes a pin check fail on a mirror for the right reason.

yolov8n-pose.license_source: the MIRROR states agpl-3.0, and so does Ultralytics' own release
yolov8n-pose.verified: DOWNLOADED AND PACKED, and this is the strongest claim in the table: the packer took it unchanged (116 ops, 73 convolutions, 3.28 M params) and on docs/bus.jpg it finds the SAME THREE PEOPLE as the container this tree built, with every keypoint, every box and every score identical to 0.000 px. So for this model a mirror is not merely usable, it is indistinguishable.
yolov8n-pose.pin_note: models/yolov8n-pose.npue IS packed from this exact file -- its weights agree to 0.000 px -- but models/yolov8n-pose/ has no CHECKPOINT.json, so there is no recorded pin and no digest to check a download against. That is the gap worth closing here rather than in a mirror: the file is now named and hashed, so writing the CHECKPOINT.json is a two-minute job that this document cannot do for you.

mediapipe-hands.license_source: models/mediapipe-hands/CHECKPOINT.json -- NOT the repository, which carries no license: tag at all
mediapipe-hands.verified: BOTH downloaded and hashed. Every value in CHECKPOINT.json -- the two sha256s and both sizes -- matches the bytes HuggingFace serves today, and they match the local files.
mediapipe-hands.two_files_note: TWO checkpoints in one container, and they are not interchangeable: the landmark network is given a hand's RoI by the palm detector and cannot find a hand in a frame by itself, so shipping only it answers 'no hand here' to every image. Both files are 2023feb; the 2023feb_int8 and 2023feb_int8bq variants are in the same repositories and are DELIBERATELY NOT used -- see CHECKPOINT.json, which measures what they do to the output.
